scope: internal implementing-model review; randomized labels observed before opening key; not independent validation
review_mode: All decoded video frames inspected sequentially in ordered contact pages, with full-frame source quartiles; not timed playback perception.
observations: Across all 33 frames, B retains connected outer cymbal, stool and support contours but merges much of the central drum region. The boundary separating the left cymbal from the adjacent upper drum repeatedly opens and closes.

C retains a recognizable central drumhead loop through the sequence, a local interior feature missing from the merged B region. Its remaining cymbal/head curves and supports are mostly disconnected; the useful loop does not restore the complete kit.

A preserves some longer cymbal/stand strokes but has persistent body and support gaps. A/C broad stroke locations change smoothly over this very small camera motion, with smaller local fragment/visibility changes. D remains point-like.

No exact popping count or comparable-ink superiority is inferred from these pages. The camera change is deliberately narrow, and lower ink plus missing structures limit the meaning of apparent local stability.
